title: Steak Diane
subtitle: Pan-fried steak in a flambéed cream and mustard sauce
excerpt: A restaurant classic from the 1950s and 1960s: thin beef steaks pan-fried fast in butter, the pan deglazed with brandy and flambéed, then a quick sauce of shallots, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, and cream poured over. Theatrical and very good.

recipe.sourceNotes: Steak Diane was a tableside preparation in upscale restaurants of mid-twentieth century New York and London, where the maître d' would cook the steaks on a trolley beside the table and flambé the pan with brandy in a display of theatre and showmanship. The dish's origins are disputed: it may be named after the Roman goddess Diana, patron of the hunt, linking the dish to game meat, though by the mid-century it was invariably made with beef. The key characteristics are the thin steak (which cooks in under a minute and stays tender), the brandy flambé (which burns off alcohol and caramelises the fond), and the cream sauce fortified with Worcestershire sauce and mustard. It fell out of fashion in the 1980s but remains an excellent quick dish.

content.text: The steaks must be very thin (about 1 cm) and the pan must be extremely hot so they sear rather than steam. If you are flambéing with brandy, tilt the pan towards the flame or use a lit match; the flames will die down in 10 to 15 seconds. Do not add the cream until the flames are completely out.

items.preparation: 2 steaks; pounded or cut to 1 cm thickness

content.text: Season the steaks. Heat half the butter in a frying pan over the highest possible heat. Sear the steaks for 30 to 60 seconds per side until well browned. Remove to a warm plate.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the remaining butter, shallots, and garlic. Cook for 2 minutes. Pour in 60 ml of brandy if using and tilt the pan or hold a match to it to flambé. Let the flames subside completely.

Add the beef stock and Worcestershire sauce. Stir and reduce for 1 minute. Add the mustard and cream. Stir over medium heat for 2 minutes until slightly thickened. Return the steaks and any juices. Turn to coat in the sauce. Scatter with parsley and serve immediately.
